items.cite: Hugh Cobbe (ed.), *Letters of Ralph Vaughan Williams 1895–1958* (Oxford University Press, 2008; paperback 2010).
items.note: Some 750 letters, selected from about 3,300 then known and arranged chronologically, covering Vaughan Williams’s musical, personal and political concerns, including his music, his war service and his friends. The Vaughan Williams Foundation’s online database now holds over 5,000.

items.cite: Vaughan Williams Foundation, *The Letters of Ralph Vaughan Williams* (searchable database of over 5,000 items).
items.note: Each transcript gives the date, the recipient, the location of the original and the page in Cobbe’s edition, so that a quotation can be checked against the whole correspondence.

items.cite: Ursula Vaughan Williams, *R.V.W.: A Biography of Ralph Vaughan Williams* (Oxford University Press, 1964).
items.note: His widow’s biography records the composer’s life as the household remembered it, from the origins of the Pastoral Symphony at Écoivres to the paragraph in The Times behind the Fourth. The Foundation calls it a key study and a mine of information.

items.cite: Michael Kennedy, *The Works of Ralph Vaughan Williams* (Oxford University Press, second edition 1980).
items.note: An account of his musical life, with a select list of works in chronological order and their first performances.

items.cite: Michael Kennedy, *A Catalogue of the Works of Ralph Vaughan Williams* (Oxford University Press, second edition 1996).
items.note: The standard catalogue of his music and writings, giving the dates, scoring and first performances of each piece, published or unpublished.

items.cite: Alain Frogley and Aidan J. Thomson (eds), *The Cambridge Companion to Vaughan Williams* (Cambridge University Press, 2013).
items.note: Essays by specialists, including one on his large choral works and the British festival tradition.
